To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have isolated nearly full length cDNA clones of bovine and murine terminal deoxynucelotidyltransferases (TdT); (2) these cDNAs were cloned into a mammalian expression vector, and the resulting plasmids were transfected into monkey cells; (3) the monkey cells expressed TdT protein which was detected by immunological and enzymatic means; (4) the expressed TdT was localized in the nuclei of monkey cells;

the bovine and mouse TdT cDNAs have been cloned and expressed as enzymatically active TdT protein in mammalian cells, and that the N-terminal nuclear localization sequence is conserved in these two mammalian cDNA sequences.
we have isolated nearly full length cDNA clones of bovine and murine TdT, expressed the bovine cDNA clone in COS7 cells, and demonstrated that the protein was localized in the cell nucleus.

The main takeaway from our work is that
TdT is an enzyme with a nuclear localization sequence, that the sequence is conserved among species, and that it is necessary for nuclear localization.
the TdT protein expressed in mammalian cells is enzymatically active and that the N-terminal region of TdT may play an important role in the intracellular localization of this enzyme.
the pcD vector expression system provides an excellent means of expressing TdT cDNA in mammalian cells for biochemical and immunological characterization of the protein.
